about: Every text the Kotlin backend's Lua engine REFUSES, and why each one is a
refusal rather than a gap.
`LuaScriptEngine` offers the author's ECMAScript to `sce-build`'s frontend,
and what the frontend will not lower is refused — W3C SCXML §scxml-5.9.1,
the processor places `error.execution` on the internal queue. Until
2026-08-30 it was handed to `EcmaScriptToLuaTransformer` instead and
guessed at; that unit is retired and this file is what replaced the number
measuring the distance to its retirement.
WHY A LIST AND NOT A COUNT. The count it replaced was a ceiling over the
fallback's uses, driven down to zero. A ceiling cannot work here for two
separate reasons and both are worth stating. First, `rewriter=0` became
STRUCTURAL the day the unit was deleted — nothing in this tree can move
that number, and a predicate nothing can move is not a measurement.
Second, a refusal is not by itself a defect: a suite that asks for `foo`
with nothing named `foo` gets exactly what the clause requires, so `how
many` cannot separate the specification working from a shape the frontend
should learn. WHICH ONES can.
HELD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS by `scripts/gates/w3c-kotlin.sh`, which reads the
census the engine writes. A refused text with no entry here is RED — an
unclassified refusal is a gap nobody looked at. An entry no run produces is
RED too: a list that keeps a case it no longer describes cannot be trusted
in the other direction either.
THE LIST GOES DOWN. Each entry is one of three things, and its `why` says
which: a shape the frontend should learn (the entry leaves when it does), a
caller handing Lua through the ECMAScript door (the entry leaves when the
caller re-tags), or the specification's own refusal (the entry stays, and
cites the clause). Adding an entry of either of the first two kinds is a
claim to argue in `docs/SCE_LUA_TRANSLATION_SEAM.md`, not a way to make
this lane green.
`text` is the AUTHOR'S spelling — `ScriptSource.source`, the text the
document wrote — and not the lowering, because a refusal has no lowering.
`produced_by` NAMES WHAT REACHES IT, and it is what keeps the rest of an
entry from being a story. Every `why` below claims some case exercises its
text; until this field existed nothing re-read that claim, and a sentence
nobody re-reads is the kind this repository has watched rot twice already.
So each entry names its producers and the gate RESOLVES every name against
the tree: a run of digits must be a fixture that
`tests/w3c/conformance/fixtures.json` registers, and anything else must be
a Kotlin test class that exists under
`backends/kotlin/tests/src/test/kotlin`. A name that is neither is RED,
never skipped — retiring test307 has to take this file's `Var1` entry with
it rather than leaving behind a reason no reader can follow.
⚠ What it does NOT prove, stated rather than hidden: that the named case
is the one that produced the text ON THIS RUN. The census records the text
and not its caller, so the honest strength of this field is that every
producer named still exists. The `unseen` direction covers the rest — a
text no run produces is red however well its producers are spelled — and
the two together are why neither alone would do.
⚠⚠ A refusal can be raised at BUILD time on one artifact and at RUN time
on another, from the same document. The generator lowers against what the
DOCUMENT declares; the engine's run-time frontend is handed the SESSION's
scope. Three of the entries below are only reached over an ECMAScript
artifact for that reason, which is why the census this file is matched
against is the one accumulated across ALL of `KOTLIN_ENGINE_PAIRS` rather
than any single pair's.

why: `never_declared` is a name the session's scope has never been told
about, so the frontend refuses the expression and the engine reports
it. That is what the clause asks for — an expression the datamodel
cannot evaluate places `error.execution` on the internal queue — and
it is what `DatamodelReadJsonTest` asks the engine for on purpose:
the reader must answer null for a `<data>` that is not there rather
than invent a value for it.
THIS ENTRY DOES NOT LEAVE. It is the one kind of refusal that is not
a gap: no shape the frontend could learn would make an undeclared
name resolvable, because resolving it is exactly what the clause
forbids.
A Lua table constructor with a bracketed key, handed through the
ECMAScript door ON PURPOSE. It is the control half of
`ScriptLanguageSeamTest.theLoweredScriptArmSkipsTheRunTimeLoweringToo`:
the same characters tagged `lua` must reach the interpreter as
written, and the same characters tagged `ecmascript` must NOT, or the
tag changed nothing and the case measures one path twice.
⚠ What the control observes NARROWED when
`EcmaScriptToLuaTransformer` was retired, and it got stronger. The
rewriter used to mangle this text into something that ran and left no
readable `o.k`; the frontend refuses it, which the same assertion
reads as the same 'not 7'. A wrong answer and a refusal are both 'the
tag was not ignored', and only the refusal is what the clause wants.
THIS ENTRY DOES NOT LEAVE EITHER, for as long as that case does: it
is a deliberate mis-tag, not a shape the frontend should learn. A
frontend that accepted it would be parsing Lua as ECMAScript.
The guard the W3C IRP suite writes where its `conf:nonBoolean`
placeholder goes. test344 states the requirement in its own comment —
the placeholder "will have to be mapped onto something that produces a
syntax error or something similarly invalid" — and a reserved word used
as a value is that invalid thing. test309 asks for the same from the
other side: "an expression that cannot be interpreted as a boolean is
treated as false".
So the frontend refusing it is the test passing. An ECMAScript frontend
that accepted `return` as an expression would have stopped being one,
which is why this is not a shape to learn.
⚠ It reaches the census only over an ECMAScript artifact. Generating
the same document for Lua moves the refusal to BUILD time — the guard
is emitted as `error("…reserved word 'return' used as a value…")` — so
the committed machines carry the refusal as text and never ask the
engine for it. Both routes land on this clause; only one lands at run
time.
THIS ENTRY DOES NOT LEAVE while test309 and test344 are registered.
test343 — "test that illegal <param> produces error.execution and empty
event.data" — carries `<param location="foo" name="someParam"/>` in a
document that never declares `foo`. Reading it is the illegal act the
test is built on, so the refusal is the expected result rather than a
gap standing in front of one.
⚠ Both artifacts refuse it, and in the same place: the generator's
frontend declines at build time too and emits `error("SCXML expr is not
valid ECMAScript: foo: foo is not declared by this document")`. Two
routes agreeing is what a specification refusal should look like.
THIS ENTRY DOES NOT LEAVE while test343 is registered.
test307 is the `binding="late"` test and its comment states the shape:
"in s0 we access a variable that isn't created until we get to s1".
Late binding means `Var1` is not in the session's scope when s0's `<log
expr="Var1"/>` runs, so an ECMAScript datamodel owes a ReferenceError
there and the engine reports one.
⚠⚠ This is the entry where the two artifacts DIVERGE, and the
divergence is the binding rule rather than a defect. The generator
lowers against what the DOCUMENT declares — every `<data id>` in it,
whenever bound — so over the committed Lua machines `Var1` lowers to
`Var1` and the same ReferenceError arrives one step later, from
`LuaScriptEngine.isUndeclaredSimpleVariable`, off the interpreter's own
globals. Over the ECMAScript artifact the run-time frontend is handed
the SESSION's scope, which does not hold `Var1` yet, and refuses. One
clause, one observable event, two places it can be raised.
⚠ `Var1` is the suite's most common variable name and almost every
other document declares it early, so almost none of them refuse it —
test342 evaluates this very text as a `<send eventexpr>` and is NOT
refused. The late-bound read is the one that is, which is why this
entry names test307 alone.
THIS ENTRY DOES NOT LEAVE while test307 is registered.
